data.narrative:
Cambridge Aerospace, a Series B-stage defense and security company founded by Steven Barrett and Chris Sylvan, has raised $300M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 10 peers—2 public and 8 private—operating in the same sector and stage, including Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Defense Unicorns ($1.0B), and Heven AeroTech ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods apply to this target. The stage-progression method uses the $300M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding $570M. The peer-median method establishes valuation from the six same-sector, same-stage comparables, which cluster at a $1.1B median with a $300M floor and $3.0B ceiling. This dispersion reflects material variance in growth profiles and defensibility within the peer set.

Synthesizing both methods produces a triangulated range of $484M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $848M. The gap between stage-progression and peer-median results—$570M versus $1.1B—reflects uncertainty around whether Cambridge Aerospace's capital efficiency and market position track toward the lower or median quartile of its peer cohort. Resolution of this range depends on visibility into revenue scale, unit economics, and customer concentration relative to the identified comparables.
